title: A kept-client Reconnect whose browser never opened is locked for ten minutes
body:
## Summary
After a one-press Reconnect (ADR 0117) the Accounts panel disables Reconnect while the flow waits, and the kept-client flow has no consent link, so a browser that did not open leaves the person stuck until the flow's 600 s TTL.

## Description
ADR 0117 (docs/adr/0117-a-reconnect-reuses-the-sealed-client-and-no-client-value-crosses-the-route.md, Consequences) says: "If the browser did not open, the person presses Reconnect again, or uses a different client." The panel does not allow either. `apps/desktop/src/scenes/accounts/view.tsx:628` sets `consentOpen` whenever `busy || waiting`, and `:727` hands it to Reconnect as its disabledReason ("A consent page is open; finish it in the browser first."); "Use a different client" swaps to the two fields, whose Connect is disabled by the same `consentOpen` (`:771`). The "Open the consent page again" link is drawn only when `flow.authorize_url` is set (`:710`), and a kept-client flow leaves it empty by design (ADR 0117 decision 3). The daemon would accept a second connect: a new flow replaces the open one for the same connector (`src/athena/connectors/oauth.py:255-266`). The flow runs out after `FLOW_TTL_S = 600.0` (`src/athena/connectors/oauth.py:38`). Technique: async-ui-states action-busy-states (a pressed control acknowledges the work, and the person keeps a way out). Fixed looks like: while a kept-client flow waits, Reconnect stays pressable as "Open Google again" (or similar), a second press starts a fresh flow, and the store's `pollFlow` is single-flight per connector so two polls never race their `busy` marks (`apps/desktop/src/stores/connectors.ts` pollFlow today has no guard; it is unreachable only because the button is disabled).

## Flow
- Gmail needs reconnecting, its client is kept: Accounts shows Reconnect
- press Reconnect -> connect(id, {reuse_client:true}) -> the daemon opens the browser itself; the store polls with busy "waiting for consent"
- the browser did not open (default browser blocked, focus elsewhere) -> the panel says "waiting for consent", no link, Reconnect disabled
- observed: nothing to press for up to 10 minutes; ADR 0117 promised Reconnect again
- fix in build order: interact test red (Reconnect pressable while a kept flow waits; a second press sends one more connect and the store polls once), pollFlow single-flight in stores/connectors.ts, the view's disabledReason for the kept arm

## Expected impact
Every self-registered Gmail user who reconnects weekly and whose browser did not come forward; today they wait out the TTL or restart. Measured by the interact test. Could break: two concurrent flows if the store guard is skipped.

## Evaluation
Claim: user - a reconnect whose browser did not open can be retried at once, as ADR 0117 says
Before: the walked case: Reconnect disabled with "finish it in the browser first" and no link for the flow's 600 s TTL (view.tsx:628, :710, :727; oauth.py:38)
After: predicted: a second press starts a new flow (oauth.py:255-266 replaces the old one); one poll per connector
Method: simulation - walked from the view, the store and the daemon's flow table; the fix's view half is in desktop-scenes-accounts-apps, outside this round's paths, so no gate was run
Result: better
Gate: none
instrument: scenes/accounts/interact.test.tsx: a needs-reauth kept row with flow awaiting_consent and authorize_url "" -> Reconnect enabled, a press calls connect once more; stores/connectors.test.ts: two pollFlow calls for one id make one poll loop

title: A row's error is titled "Gmail refused." when the request never reached the daemon
body:
## Summary
The list's problem says whether the daemon refused or the request never left (`ConnectorProblem.from`); a row's error does not, and Accounts titles every row error "<Label> refused.", including a fetch that failed and the store's own "the daemon is not ready".

## Description
`apps/desktop/src/stores/connectors.ts` `problemOf` (:132-137) attributes a list failure to `daemon` only for an `ApiError`, because "The vault said no" and "we never asked" send a reader to different machines (`apps/desktop/src/modules/connectors/model.ts:352-367`). Row acts go through `fail` (:167-168), which keeps `reasonOf` alone, and `act` writes a client sentence "the daemon is not ready" into the same map (:176-179), documented as "the daemon's own words" (model.ts:85, connectors.ts:78). `apps/desktop/src/scenes/accounts/view.tsx:231` and `:513` draw every row error as `<ProblemNote title={`${row.label} refused.`} ...>`. So a `TypeError: Failed to fetch` on Probe reads "Gmail refused. Failed to fetch". Technique: async-ui-states failure-states ("distinguish the failure classes the user can act on differently: unreachable vs rejected"). Fixed: the store keeps `from` per row error as it does for the list, the row carries it, and the view titles a client failure "Athena could not reach the daemon." (or similar).

## Flow
- Accounts, a connected Gmail row, press Probe while the daemon is restarting
- act -> deps.api() null -> fail(id, "the daemon is not ready"), or the fetch throws TypeError
- observed: "Gmail refused." over "the daemon is not ready" / "Failed to fetch"
- fix in build order: store test (TypeError -> errorFrom client; ApiError -> daemon), row field, view test on the title

## Expected impact
Anyone whose daemon blinks while acting on an account; they read Gmail as refusing them. Measured by a store and a view test. Could break: the view tests that pin "refused." titles for daemon refusals (kept).

## Evaluation
Claim: quality - a row error says who answered, as the list's problem already does
Before: 3 sources of row error (ApiError, TypeError, the store's not-ready sentence), 1 title for all: "<Label> refused." (view.tsx:231, :513)
After: predicted: 2 titles, chosen by from; ApiError keeps "refused."
Method: simulation - three cases walked through act/fail and the view; the title lives in scenes/accounts/view.tsx (another context), so no gate was run here
Result: better
Gate: none
instrument: stores/connectors.test.ts: probe with a throwing fetch -> errorFrom.notion === "client"; scenes/accounts/view.test.tsx: a row with a client error is not titled "refused."

title: The one-press Reconnect state has no fixture a preview or a view test can reach
body:
## Summary
No connectors fixture carries `client_kept: true`, and the Accounts fixtures pick module fixtures by name, so the ADR 0117 Reconnect panel cannot be opened in `preview.html` and no markup test draws it.

## Description
`apps/desktop/src/modules/connectors/fixtures.ts:199-212` (`needs-reauth`) has no `client_kept`, so `rowOf` sets `reconnect: false` (`apps/desktop/src/modules/connectors/model.ts` rowOf, `view.client_kept === true`). `apps/desktop/src/scenes/accounts/fixtures.ts:63-77` lists the module fixtures it reuses by hand, so a new module fixture would not appear either. The only coverage of the Reconnect markup is `apps/desktop/src/scenes/accounts/interact.test.tsx:201`, which patches `reconnect: true` onto rows by hand. The brief for this run notes the Reconnect state was never seen in the real window; a preview fixture is the cheap way to look at it. Fixed: a module fixture `needs-reauth-kept` (and one with its flow waiting), listed in the Accounts fixtures and PLACES, with a view test drawing "Reconnect" and "Use a different client".

## Flow
- open preview.html?scene=accounts&fixture=needs-reauth&at=... -> the two client fields, never Reconnect
- fix in build order: module fixture with client_kept, accounts fixtures/PLACES entries, view.test markup case

## Expected impact
Whoever reviews the Reconnect panel in a browser or the perf gate; today it exists only in an interact test's patched rows. Could break: nothing (fixtures only).

## Evaluation
Claim: quality - the Reconnect state is reachable in the preview and pinned by a markup test
Before: 0 fixtures with reconnect: true (grep client_kept in fixtures: 0); 0 view.test cases for Reconnect
After: predicted: 1 fixture, 1 place, 1 markup case
Method: probe - grep over src/**/fixtures.ts for client_kept (0 hits) and accounts fixtures' hand-kept module list; the accounts half is another context's file
Result: better
Gate: none
instrument: scenes/accounts/view.test.tsx: place("open-reauth-kept") contains ">Reconnect<" and "Use a different client"

title: run.ts keeps its own originOf, so a "null" origins row still trusts every blank and file page
body:
## Summary
4fcb054 made the Browser module's `originOf` answer "" for an opaque origin, so register can no longer write a "null" row; `stores/run.ts` and `companion/tools.ts` keep their own copies that answer "null", and `openTabOf` trusts a tab whose origin is "null" when such a row exists.

## Description
Three implementations of one rule: `apps/desktop/src/modules/browser/model.ts` originOf (now "" for opaque), `apps/desktop/src/stores/run.ts:1884-1890` and `apps/desktop/src/companion/tools.ts:50-56` (both `new URL(url).origin`, so "null"). `apps/desktop/src/stores/run.ts:258-264` `openTabOf` computes `trusted` as `origin !== "" && ... origins.known.includes(origin) && enabled`, so a "null" row written before 4fcb054 (or by any other writer) trusts every about:blank, file: and data: tab at once. Three scene callers each re-check `origin !== "null"` by hand (scenes/apps/model.ts:82, scenes/apps/view.tsx:226, scenes/chores/live.tsx:30, scenes/waking/view.tsx:82). Fixed: one `originOf` (lib/url.ts) that answers "" for opaque origins, used by all, and `openTabOf` never trusting ""; a parity test pins it.

## Flow
- a store that holds an origins row "null" (written by the old register path)
- an about:blank or file: tab -> run.ts originOf -> "null" -> known.includes("null") -> trusted
- fix in build order: openTabOf test with a "null" row and an about:blank tab (trusted false), one originOf in lib/url.ts, callers moved

## Expected impact
Anyone who pressed Register this app on a blank or file page before 4fcb054. Measured by the run.ts test. Could break: the scene callers' item keys (they already treat "null" as none).

## Evaluation
Claim: quality - one origin rule; an opaque page is never trusted by a row
Before: 3 originOf implementations, 2 answering "null"; openTabOf trusts a "null" row (walked)
After: predicted: 1 implementation; trusted false for opaque tabs
Method: simulation - walked from the code; run.ts and companion/tools.ts are other contexts' files
Result: better
Gate: policy-tighten
instrument: stores/run.test.ts: openTabOf("about:blank", [blank tab], {}, table with an enabled "null" row).trusted === false

title: A connector card for a grant whose last probe was broken names the account and warns of nothing
body:
## Summary
`connectorLineOf` warns only of causes the gate will refuse (lapsed grant, not connected, switched off, writes off); a connected Gmail whose last probe answered 401 reads "Acts as mira@example.com through Gmail." with no hint the send is likely to fail after the signature.

## Description
`apps/desktop/src/modules/connectors/model.ts:176-179` ranks the causes; `connection.health === "broken"` is not one. Accounts paints the same record red (`standingOf`, model.ts:282-290: "broken (3 min ago)" with the provider's detail). ADR 0116 decision 1 fixed the cause list and its sentence ", so approving now will be refused.", which would be untrue for broken (the gate does not refuse; the provider does, after the signature). Adding it means a second warning kind with its own words ("Gmail answered 401 at the last check; this may fail after you approve.") and amends ADR 0116. Technique: hitl-approval (the card states what the approver needs to decide).

## Flow
- Accounts shows Gmail broken (401, 3 min ago)
- a send_mail card arrives in her window -> connectorLineOf -> no warning
- the person approves -> the call fails as could-not-carry-out after the signature

## Expected impact
Whoever approves a send on a broken grant. Measured by a model test once the wording is decided. Could break: a stale broken verdict warning on a grant that has since recovered (the probe age would have to be shown).

## Evaluation
Claim: user - the card says what Accounts already says about the grant before the signature
Before: 1 of 5 standings (broken) shown in Accounts and silent on the card
After: predicted: 0 silent, with a non-refusal wording
Method: simulation - walked from connectorLineOf and standingOf; the wording and whether a prediction belongs on the card is a product call that amends ADR 0116
Result: unmeasurable
Gate: direction
